title: BACE: Biotechnology Skills (Practical) - Biotechnology Skills - Aseptic Technique
subject: Biotechnology Skills

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the primary purpose of aseptic technique in a biotechnology laboratory?
options: To ensure all equipment is cleaned with soap and water before use.
To prevent contamination of the culture, the environment, and the researcher.
To sterilize all solutions using high heat and pressure immediately after use.
To increase the growth rate of the bacterial culture being studied.
questions.explain: Aseptic technique is a set of practices used to prevent the introduction of contamination (unwanted microbes) into samples, the sterile field, or the researcher.
questions.subject: Biotechnology Skills

questions.q: What are the standard conditions for sterilizing liquid media in an autoclave?
options: 100°C at 0 psi for 60 minutes
121°C at 15 psi for 15-20 minutes
150°C at 30 psi for 5 minutes
200°C at 10 psi for 45 minutes
questions.explain: The standard autoclave cycle for sterilizing liquids is 121°C at 15 psi pressure for approximately 15 to 20 minutes.
questions.subject: Biotechnology Skills

questions.q: When working in a laminar flow hood, where should you perform your work to minimize contamination?
options: At the very front edge of the hood, closest to the user.
Outside the hood, transferring items in only when necessary.
At least 6 inches inside the hood, in the center of the sterile airflow.
Against the back wall of the hood to avoid air turbulence.
questions.explain: Work should be performed at least 6 inches inside the hood to ensure that the air flow is laminar and undisturbed by the turbulence at the front opening or the back obstruction.
questions.subject: Biotechnology Skills

questions.q: Which of the following actions represents a violation of aseptic technique?
options: Flaming the mouth of a glass tube before and after transferring a sample.
Placing a sterile cap face-down on the lab bench while pipetting.
Holding the test tube at an angle while the cap is removed.
Using a fresh, sterile pipette tip for each transfer.
questions.explain: Placing a sterile cap face-down on a non-sterile surface (like a lab bench) introduces contamination. Caps should be held in the hand or placed face-up if absolutely necessary, though holding is preferred.
questions.subject: Biotechnology Skills

questions.q: Identify the correct order of steps for aseptically transferring a bacterial culture from a tube to a fresh broth tube.
options: Flame loop $\rightarrow$ Remove cap $\rightarrow$ Flame tube lip $\rightarrow$ Obtain sample $\rightarrow$ Flame tube lip $\rightarrow$ Recap
Remove cap $\rightarrow$ Flame loop $\rightarrow$ Obtain sample $\rightarrow$ Flame tube lip $\rightarrow$ Recap
Flame tube lip $\rightarrow$ Flame loop $\rightarrow$ Remove cap $\rightarrow$ Obtain sample $\rightarrow$ Recap
Obtain sample $\rightarrow$ Flame loop $\rightarrow$ Flame tube lip $\rightarrow$ Remove cap $\rightarrow$ Recap
questions.explain: The correct sequence ensures sterility at every exposure point: Sterilize the tool (loop), open the container, sterilize the air-interface (lip), perform transfer, re-sterilize the interface, and close.
questions.subject: Biotechnology Skills

questions.q: What is the function of the Bunsen burner flame during tube-to-tube transfers?
options: To heat the liquid culture to boiling point.
To create an updraft that pushes airborne contaminants away from the open tube.
To illuminate the workspace.
To burn off excess oxygen in the tube.
questions.explain: Besides sterilizing loops, the flame heats the air, causing it to rise (convection). This updraft helps prevent airborne dust and microbes from falling into open containers near the flame.
questions.subject: Biotechnology Skills

questions.q: Which Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) is most essential for protecting the *sample* from contamination by the researcher's skin flora?
options: Safety goggles
Gloves
Closed-toe shoes
Fire extinguisher
questions.explain: Gloves cover the skin of the hands, which sheds skin cells and bacteria, thus protecting the sample from the researcher's flora. Goggles and shoes primarily protect the researcher.
questions.subject: Biotechnology Skills

questions.q: You observe a broth culture that was supposed to be sterile but now appears cloudy (turbid). What is the most likely conclusion?
options: The broth has evaporated.
The broth is contaminated with microbial growth.
The pH of the broth has spontaneously changed.
The broth was over-sterilized.
questions.explain: Turbidity (cloudiness) in a liquid medium is a classic visual sign of microbial growth (contamination).
questions.subject: Biotechnology Skills

questions.q: What is the correct method for sterilizing an inoculating loop in a Bunsen burner flame?
options: Pass it quickly through the yellow part of the flame once.
Hold it in the blue cone of the flame until it glows red hot along the entire wire.
Hold it in the flame for exactly 3 seconds, regardless of color.
Dip it in ethanol and then waive it near the flame to dry.
questions.explain: The loop must be heated until it glows red hot to ensure all organic matter and microbes are incinerated. The blue cone is the hottest part of the flame.
questions.subject: Biotechnology Skills

questions.q: Why must you wait for the inoculating loop to cool after flaming before touching a bacterial colony?
options: The hot loop will melt the agar and ruin the plate.
The hot loop will kill the bacteria you are trying to pick up.
The hot loop will cause the bacteria to mutate.
The hot loop will cause aerosols that contaminate the air.
questions.explain: Touching a live culture with a red-hot loop will instantly kill the cells (sizzle sound), resulting in no viable transfer.
questions.subject: Biotechnology Skills

questions.q: Which agent is commonly used to wipe down lab benches before and after work to reduce microbial load?
options: Distilled water
70% Ethanol or Isopropanol
100% Ethanol
Saline solution
questions.explain: 70% alcohol is more effective than 100% because the presence of water helps the alcohol penetrate the cell walls of microbes and denature proteins.
questions.subject: Biotechnology Skills

questions.q: In a scenario where a pipette tip accidentally touches the lab bench, what is the correct corrective action?
options: Wipe the tip with a Kimwipe and continue.
Dip the tip in ethanol and continue.
Discard the tip immediately and attach a new sterile one.
Flame the plastic tip briefly.
questions.explain: Plastic tips are disposable. Once contaminated (touched non-sterile surface), they must be discarded to maintain asepsis. They cannot be flamed (they melt) or reliably wiped.
